chunks: Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Jareer al-Qummi, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: “May I be sacrificed for you, you have known my devotion to your father, then to you. Then I swore to him, by the right of Rasool Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the right of so-and-so and so-and-so, until I ended with him, that whatever you inform me of will not go out from me to anyone among the people.”

And I asked him about his father: “Is he alive or dead?” So he said: “By Allah, he has died.” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, your Shi'a narrate that in him is the sunnah of four Prophets.” He said: “By Allah, other than Whom there is no god, he has perished.” I said: “A perishing of occultation or a perishing of death?” He said: “A perishing of death.”

So I said: “Perhaps you are practicing taqiyyah with me.” He said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “Did he appoint you by وصية?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Did he include anyone with you in it?” He said: “No.” I said: “Is there an Imam over you from among your brothers?” He said: “No.” I said: “So you are the Imam?” He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he bequeathed or designated through وصية
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely designated religious authority and leader
key_terms.انْقِطَاعِي: my exclusive devotion and turning away from others toward the Imam
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation for protection under sensitive circumstances
key_terms.سُنَّةَ: a characteristic pattern or precedent attributed here to Prophets
key_terms.غَيْبَةٍ: occultation or absence from public view
key_terms.هَلَاكَ: passing away or perishing, clarified in the report as actual death

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith establish the death of the previous Imam and the designation of the next Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith records Abu Jareer al-Qummi’s direct questioning of Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام regarding the death of his father and the transfer of the Imamate. The Imam عليه السلام explicitly affirms that his father died an actual death, not a ghaybah, and confirms that the وصية came specifically to him, establishing his singular status as Imam.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abu Jareer Al Qummy who said, 
‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, (8<sup>th</sup> Imam) <sup>asws</sup>‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> have known of my cutting-off (from others) to your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, then to you<sup>asws</sup>. Then I took an oath to him<sup>asws</sup> by the right of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and the right of so and so, and so and so, until I ended up to him<sup>asws</sup>, with that, ‘Whatever you<sup>asws</sup> inform me with would not be coming out from me to anyone from the people’. 
And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘Is he<sup>asws</sup> alive or has he<sup>asws</sup> passed away?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> has passed away’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Your<sup>asws</sup> Shias are reporting that in him<sup>asws</sup> were the Sunnahs of four Prophets<sup>as</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, there being no god except Him<sup>azwj</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> has passed away!’. I said, ‘Passing away of absence (Occultation) or passing away of death?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Passing away of death’.
So I said, ‘Perhaps you are observing dissimulation from me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’ I said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed to you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘So did he<sup>asws</sup> participate anyone else in it with you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘So is there an Imam<sup>asws</sup> over you<sup>asws</sup> from your<sup>asws</sup> brethren?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘So you<sup>asws</sup> are the Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from abu Hariz al-Qummi who has said the following.

“I said to abu al-Hassan (a.s.), ‘May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, you know how devoted I have been towards your father and after him to yourself. I then swore before him up on the rights of the Messenger of Allah and the rights of so and so and so and so (Ali, al-Hassan, al-Husayn . (a.s.) until his own self trying to assure him that whatever you would tell me will not be made public and spread to other people.

I asked him about his father to find out if he alive or dead.” He said, “by Allah, he that his father had passed away.” I then said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, your followers (Shi‘a) narrate that in him the traditions of four prophets are found.” He then said, “In certainty by Allah, besides whom there is no Lord that he (my father) has passed away.” I asked, “Is his passing away in the form of disappearance or in the form of death?” He then said, “It is in the form of death.”

I then said, “Perhaps you are observing cautious fear from me.” He said, “All glory belongs to Allah, (that is not the case).” I then asked, “Did he deliver his will to you?” He said, “Yes, he did so.” I then asked, “Has he made others as your partners in executing his will?” He said, “No, he has not done so.” I then asked, “Is there any Imam over you among your brothers?” He said, “No, there is no one from them.” I then asked, “Are you the Imam (a.s.)?” He said, “Yes, I am the Imam (Leadership with Divine Authority).”
